items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: Played down there with, uh, Bebe Ridgely.

ctx.x: No, Zeb's dead. The guy I really liked to hear play clarinet. He played such a sweet clarinet. It was, uh, a fellow by the name of Watson. Used to play with Sam Morgan. I used to like to hear him play clarinet. And he used to like to hear me play. Because the OAC, he wanted me to blow. And I, you know, I'd just rather hear him play than play myself. He didn't make so much, but what he made was so pretty and clean. Real fine clarinet player. I went down to, uh, Pete Herman's. Played down there with, uh, Bebe…

I was playing clarinet. I was doing clarinet. And what about the name of Earl? His name was Earl Trusclair. He's the first man that ever showed me any finger on a saxophone. We alternated. He showed me my finger on the saxophone and I showed him his finger on the clarinet. And that's the only thing anybody ever showed me about a saxophone. Oh, no. Nobody never showed me nothing about a clarinet, but on the saxophone, that's the only fella ever showed me anything. He showed me how to finger it. And other than…
